name: Styrenix Performance Materials Ltd
title: Styrenix Performance Materials Ltd - 506222 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA ₹128 cr at 15.3% margin on mix and opportunistic pricing, but India GPPS volumes fell and management gave no numeric guidance and no new PS capacity timeline, with ABS capacity "second half" unchanged.

utilisation.quote: we still need to increase our capacity utilization to the levels we have earlier indicated

capex.peers_comment: Management said a large Korean competitor exited styrene integration and that Korea has structurally worse quality problems; no capacity comment on peers.
capex.quote: the capex is happening exactly as we spoke

triggers.label: Profit lift partly opportunistic, not sustainable
triggers.quote: that could be also a little bit opportunistic on our part for certain segments, and that I don't think is sustainable long-term

triggers.label: GPPS volumes fell on imports and muted demand
triggers.quote: There has been a dip in our GPPS sales for the quarter. There has been a muted demand and also there has been a lot of pricing pressure on account of certain imports.

triggers.label: PS expansion back-ended, no timeline
triggers.quote: we haven't given any fresh inputs recently in terms of when this expansion would take place

triggers.label: Phase 1 ABS capacity in H2 FY27, Q3–Q4
triggers.quote: So, like I mentioned, second half would not be the first and second quarter. It would be in the third and fourth quarter.

guidance.quote: we are still saying in the second half of this year, we will have additional volumes and capacities coming in line
once we have 60%, 70% capacity utilization, the Thailand operation will start generating some returns

red_flags.label: Thailand volumes down 20-30% YoY; 'Jan to March' explanation
red_flags.quote: some 20%, 30% dip into the Thailand business

red_flags.label: Management declines volume and power savings quantification
Guidance withheld on demand and volumes

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores and PAT rose 58.6% to INR84.3 crores, despite total income down 6.3%.
summary.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income fell 6.3% to INR658 crores while EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores, with margin up 734 bps to 19.2%. Management attributed the stronger profitability to product mix (lower GPPS volumes) and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, and said there was no significant inventory gain. Volumes fell 4.6% YoY to 46.1 KT, driven by GPPS weakness, while ABS and HIPS grew. Management declined to quantify the Thailand breakeven change or the power-savings benefit, citing short-term market distortion from the Middle East supply crisis, and reiterated that India ABS capacity additions remain on track for the second half of FY27.

financial_highlights.change: up 58.6% YoY; PAT margin 12.8%, up 524 bps

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Grew YoY in Q4 volume per management; 60-70% of ABS volume is formula or contract based. ABS capacity expansion reaffirmed on schedule for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4).

segments.name: HIPS (India)
segments.commentary: Volume grew YoY in Q4; formula/OEM-based share now well above 50% of HIPS business. Capex decision on a dedicated HIPS plant still under study.

segments.name: GPPS (India)
segments.commentary: Significant volume decline in Q4 due to muted demand, unorganized market, and import dumping; Styrenix chose not to chase low-price volume. Capacity already expanded but under-utilised. Formula-based share above 70% across GPPS business.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Volumes fell 20-30% YoY in Q4 per analyst, partly due to customer pre-buying in the prior-year Jan-Mar quarter ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch. Management says most business retained; breakeven requires 60-70% utilisation.

guidance_outlook: ABS capacity additions and related capex remain on track for H2 FY27, with commissioning expected in Q3 and Q4 and no change in timelines; exact months not disclosed.
No cost escalation currently expected for the upcoming ABS capex.
Third-party power sourcing expected to start around next month; management called the timing and savings uncertain and gave no quantification.
Management declined to give FY27 volume or power-saving quantification, citing demand contraction from price increases and the Middle East situation.
Thailand breakeven stays at 60-70% utilisation; management said short-term gains from market tightness should not change the long-term target.
Management expects India ABS/SAN output to double over time; import substitution opportunity of 30,000-50,000 tonnes annual demand growth cited for the next 5-7 years.
capex_capacity: ABS capacity expansion in India remains on track for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4), per management, with no change to earlier commitments.
General-purpose polystyrene capacity was already expanded and is available, but utilisation is low due to muted demand and import pressure.
HIPS plant capex still under evaluation; no firm decision or timeline given.
PS expansion is back-ended; management will define a business case as OEM share grows.
Thailand is a small plant; management views it as a capacity source for certain technologies serving rest-of-world customers.
Consolidated versus standalone cash flow gap of about INR60 crores was raised by an analyst as implied Thailand capex; the company did not respond specifically.
demand_pricing: Indian demand was estimated at 350,000-370,000 tonnes last year; domestic players supplied about 160,000-170,000 tonnes, with nearly 200,000 tonnes imported before a third player entered.
Raw material (styrene, acrylonitrile) and finished product prices rose globally in tandem; management says there is no significant regional arbitrage.
ABS spot prices were quoted at about INR190-200 per kg versus INR110-120 pre-war, per an analyst; management said prices will likely stay somewhat higher in the short-to-medium term.
Management said Q4 profitability was helped by mix and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, which it does not view as sustainable.
Large OE customers in automotive, appliances and packaging continue to buy steadily; demand is muted at current prices and weaker among unorganized and smaller buyers.
Freight: containerized inbound freight has not moved significantly; bulk freight has softened on demand destruction in bulk petrochemicals.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Thailand breakeven utilisation (65-70%) now easier to reach given current pricing and raw material availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven targets should not change; short-term tightness gains are arbitrage that may not last. Thailand still needs to reach 60-70% utilisation to generate returns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 volume drop in India and the 20-30% drop in Thailand explained?
qa_highlights.answer: India dip was from GPPS only; ABS and HIPS grew YoY. Thailand comparison was distorted by prior-year pre-buying ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch, and Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker. Most business was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread at spot prices better or worse in FY27 versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract and formula margins are similar or slightly better. Spot margins are better for specific grades where Korean suppliers' quality is weak, but this is opportunistic.

qa_highlights.question: Should capex be preponed for ABS given Korean import disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said capex is proceeding as planned with no acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales is formula-based versus spot?
qa_highlights.answer: ABS: 60-70% formula or contract. HIPS: well above 50% formula/OEM. GPPS: formula-based pricing above 70% for the business overall, with volumes dropping as the company avoids unformulated segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thailand ever reach breakeven given normalised spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that returns start at 60-70% utilisation and the plant is still below that level.

risks_watch: Middle East supply disruption (Strait of Hormuz) and Korean petrochemical outages could change raw material costs and availability; duration unknown.
Demand contraction at elevated prices, especially in unorganized and smaller customer segments and possibly in OE customers if their inventories clear slowly.
GPPS volume trend and import pricing pressure; management is deprioritising this segment.
Timing of H2 FY27 ABS capacity commissioning and the third-party power supply start (expected around next month, unquantified).
Thailand utilisation versus the 60-70% breakeven threshold, plus the brand-transition effect on customer volumes.
Q4 margin was flattered by mix and opportunistic pricing, which management said is not sustainable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the India ABS expansion, but cautious and deliberately non-committal on near-term pricing, volumes, power savings, and margins, repeatedly citing uncertainty from the Middle East crisis. Management was candid that Q4 margin gains were partly opportunistic and that Thailand volume comparisons were distorted.
key_quotes: So, we do believe that Thailand will prove to be a very critical and important asset for the organization in terms of its positioning with these customers and also supplying to these customers in all these different regions.

I think there is obviously on the spot side, they are better because, again, for specific grade of products, we are able to supply where we are not seeing quality supplies from conventional competitors from Korea.
But that could be also a little bit opportunistic on our part for certain segments, and that I don't think is sustainable long-term.
So, to comment that your breakeven would change significantly from what we have earlier stated would be a fallacy.

adds.what: ABS capacity expansion in India (phase 1), commissioning Q3-Q4 FY27
HIPS dedicated plant in India (capex under study, no firm decision)
PS (polystyrene) expansion, back-ended, no timeline or business case yet

growth.why: Management reaffirmed India ABS capacity additions on track for Q3-Q4 FY27 with no quantification of size or capex, while declining to guide FY27 volumes; Q4 standalone total income fell 6.3% and volumes 4.6%, with EBITDA growth driven by mix and opportunistic pricing that management calls non-sustainable.
